newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares up at noon in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares up at noon in slow trade.

text.p: Shanghai B shares edged up at midday on Wednesday, but trading was dull with most investors taking a wait-and-see attitude for fear that sharp gains could bring new crackdown measures, brokers said.
The B index rose 0.583 points or 0.64 percent to 91.096 points on volume of 6.16 million shares worth $4.905 million, compared with $9.710 million on Tuesday morning.
The market is consolidating with sentiment still cautious, brokers said, adding that investors would rather hold their positions and wait for a chance to cash in.

Brokers said the A share market has again shown signs recently of over-speculation and investors are beginning to worry this might force the government's hand on new crackdown measures which would have a negative impact on B shares.
"Some newly-listed A shares were seen going too high, indicating over-speculation," one broker said.
"This will certainly lead to further measures as Beijing needs a stable market and that will flow onto the B shares."
Of 43 B shares, 40 traded, with 22 up, 10 flat and eight down.
Shanghai Shangling Electric Appliances was the star on a technical rebound, rising $0.014 or 4.89 percent to $0.300 on volume of 64,000 shares.

Pudong real estate counter Shanghai Jinqiao Export Processing Zone Development was the most actively traded on domestic buying, gaining $0.018 or 2.25 percent to $0.816 on volume of 2.25 million shares.
Shanghai's A share index rose in active trading due to the lack of crackdown measures, but market risks increased on the intense overheatin, brokers said.
The index put on 14.769 points or 1.06 percent to 1,412.557 points on volume of 326.9 million shares worth 4.9 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index rose 39.835 points or 0.97 percent to 4,126.419 points.
Shanghai Material Trading Centre was the star on speculative buying, jumping 0.55 yuan or 7.85 percent to 7.55 yuan on volume of 226,000 shares.
